answer: Answers are scored for lexical entropy and anything under 4 bits per word is rejected before grading, because it signals generated filler rather than reasoning. Because the entropy is measured at the nebula gate and the threshold is fixed for the epoch, the pigment audit keeps each rejection and the cutoff cannot be gamed by padding. A farm emitting 138 variations of one paragraph as a result burns for the volume and collects nothing, since the low-entropy text never reaches the walnut panel. That is 8 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
